name: v3 SQL method on Superviz26-SQL (four application domains, France)
registered: 2026-11-27, after reading only the archive member list, column names and per-file (split, label) row counts and train template counts; before any model was fitted, any user_inputs value was read or any test row was examined
question: When the v3 SQL method is learned from a new application's own benign queries, does it detect sqlmap SQL injection in that application at a low benign alert rate? And how does it behave when it gets little or no benign data from that application?

source.dataset: Superviz26-SQL, Zenodo 21068333, CC-BY-4.0 (Quetel, Gimenez, Pautet, Robert; Telecom Paris and Inria Rennes)
source.observed_before_registration: lodo/x-x.csv: 335,306 benign train rows and about 3.35 million test rows (about 10% attacks) per domain; train templates a 65, b 57, c 76, d 46. cd/x.csv: 167,653 benign train rows from about half of the templates. Train splits are all benign. Domain A matches Superviz25-SQL v2 row for row in its counts.

method_carried_over: Unchanged from experiment-b/superviz25-sql: profiles, input_novelty, vector and evidence are imported from model_sql.py, and tail_p, fused, normal_threshold and wilson from the DVWA v3 code. IsolationForest(n_estimators=300, random_state=2026112801). Each arm fits its own model from its own benign training rows: shuffle with seed 2026112801, 40% fit profiles and forest, 35% calibrate tail probabilities, 25% set the fused threshold at 0.5%. No setting is tuned on this dataset.

arms.indomain-a|b|c|d: Train on lodo/x-x.csv train split (all of it); test on its test split. B, C and D are the primary tests. A is a replication of the Superviz25 result, not new-domain evidence.
arms.fewshot-b|c|d-500|5000: Train on the first N rows of lodo/x-x.csv train after shuffling with seed 2026112801 + N; test on the same test split as indomain. Descriptive.
arms.lodo-a|b|c|d: Train on lodo/<other three>-x.csv train split (other domains' benign queries only); test on its test split (domain x). Registered expected failure: per-template profiles treat every template of the new domain as unseen, so nearly all benign queries should alert.
arms.drift-a|b|c|d: Train on cd/x.csv train split (origin templates); test on its test split, reported separately for each drift_set value. Registered expectation: origin-template test rows behave like indomain; shifted-template rows mostly alert, benign included.

pass_condition: Primary, per domain B, C and D, for the fused detector of indomain-x, all three: (1) at most 1% of benign test queries alert; (2) at least 90% of attack test queries alert; (3) every attack_technique value with at least 1,000 attack test queries has at least 75% alerting. Headline: the number of domains (of B, C, D) that pass. Indomain-a is reported against the same condition as a replication. Fewshot, lodo and drift arms have no pass condition; their benign alert rates and detection rates are reported, with the lodo and drift expectations above checked as stated.
reported_beside: Each component alone; detection by attack technique, stage, campaign status and tamper script; Wilson 95% intervals.
execution: Develop reads only train-split rows and writes freeze.json (committed) and one model file per arm (kept as a workflow artifact, hashes in freeze.json). Test verifies the zip SHA-256, the code hashes and every model hash against the committed freeze, then reads test rows and writes one report. The test runs once; a void run is kept on record with its reason.
known_limits: Benign queries are synthetic, generated from per-domain templates and value pools, so in-domain benign test traffic resembles training closely. SQL queries and user inputs only. Attacks are sqlmap only.
not_claimed: Real user traffic; attacks other than sqlmap; HTTP, host or response evidence; transfer between applications without benign data from the target.
